newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain ruling party hopes centre-right wins France.
newsitem.headline: Spain ruling party hopes centre-right wins France.

text.p: Spain's conservative ruling party made clear on Sunday it hopes the centre-right governing coalition in France will emerge victorious in the decisive second round of a parliamentary election next week.
French voters gave the left a substantial lead over the ruling bloc in the first round of a parliamentary election on Sunday in a stern warning to President Jacques Chirac.

"Whoever thinks the future of Europe must be passed over to a coalition between socialists and communists has not understood anything that has happened since the fall of the Berlin Wall," said Jose Maria Robles Fraga, foreign affairs representative for Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's Popular Party.

The massive protest vote after two years of austerity and record unemployment under French Prime Minister Alain Juppe threw next Sunday's decisive second-round runoff wide open and put the left within reach of a stunning upset.

Robles told reporters he was confident France's conservatives would win and form "a government which is effective in the European enterprise and in relations with Spain in such important issues as terrorism and in the resolution of such burning problems as the passage of Spanish merchants on French roads."
Spain has been delighted with a toughening stance by the French government toward Basque separatist guerrilla group ETA, which has a strong base in southern France.

But Madrid's relations with its northern neighbour have been strained in the past week over what has been dubbed a "vegetable war" -- repeated attacks by French farmers on Spanish truckers importing fruits and vegetables.
Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Sunday he had asked the European Union to impose severe sanctions on France for the damage.

Spain's leadership has accused French police of turning a blind eye while farmers, who want tighter controls on imported produce, have destroyed truckloads and warehouses full of Spanish fruits and vegetables.
